papers.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
papers.summary: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. papers.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
papers.summary: A live cross-platform benchmark evaluates computer-using agents on long-horizon workflows across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web, showing that current agents remain far from platform-robust computer use and trail humans on iOS and macOS.

papers.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
papers.summary: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. papers.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
papers.summary: A tool called Vernier measures the smallest score difference a time-series forecasting leaderboard can distinguish, showing that most boards cannot separate top entries and that ranking order can change with pool composition.

papers.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
papers.summary: A benchmark assesses how well video generators follow animated 3D blockouts while preserving structure, filling missing content, correcting proxy artifacts, and binding multimodal conditions to the correct entities and events.

papers.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
papers.summary: StateWeaver improves long-video generation by preserving cross-shot consistency and updating visual references through active state tracking and hierarchical collaboration.

papers.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
papers.summary: A fine-grained speculative streaming framework prepares action-conditioned video futures during playback to reduce input-to-display latency in interactive world models while sustaining real-time generation.

papers.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
papers.summary: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric c

papers.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: A method that explicitly shapes and expands the handoff boundary of visuomotor policies improves coordination between multimodal agents and robot policies, yielding higher success and lower cost.

papers.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
papers.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. A growing number of LLM context engineering (LCE) approaches automate the task by casting the LLM itself as the engineer that draws generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trials as context. Although these methods resemble how humans learn from experiences, it remains unclear when and how LLMs can engineer effective context from data. To answer the question, we f

papers.title: LayoutRecall: Preserving Appearance in Multi-Round 3D Layout-Controlled Image Editing
papers.summary: LayoutRecall is a multi-round 3D layout-controlled image editor that preserves object appearance across edits by storing and retrieving latents in 3D box coordinate systems and conditioning a FLUX.2 editor with geometry-aligned memory.

papers.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
papers.summary: AI agents now run statements against production databases, and several of the incidents that followed deleted production data, which came back only through backups or the provider's help. We ask what decides the damage when such an agent makes a mistake: the model, a guard layer in front of the database, or the database engine itself. The study has two preregistered layers. papers.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
papers.summary: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. papers.title: Generation as Reverse Encoding
papers.summary: A generative framework reuses a frozen encoder’s intermediate representations as staged targets and shares a DiT backbone to reduce training and sampling cost while preserving image quality.

papers.title: Reading, Not Adapting: Unlocking Frozen Visual Knowledge for AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.summary: A frozen vision foundation model can be read out through staged cross-view attention and learnable fusion queries to generalize detection across unseen image generators with very few trainable parameters.

papers.title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning
papers.summary: Conventional artificial neurons separate spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, limiting their ability to model irregular observations. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), a continuous-time primitive for replacing standard neural layers in MLPs, Transformers, and graph neural networks. DAWIN couples spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation and integrates it into a local complex state through closed-form damped evolution, avoiding numerical differential equation solvers. papers.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
papers.summary: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens. Their tokenizer must therefore preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semantic-enhanced tokenizers may lose acoustic detail, whereas acoustic-oriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that makes language modeling harder. papers.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity
papers.summary: Using frozen internal representations of tabular foundation models as financial dissimilarity measures in a spatial asset-pricing model yields positive estimated gains over direct disclosure distance once broad SEC filing data are included.

papers.title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration
papers.summary: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. However, existing 3D medical multimodal models often suffer from uncalibrated autoregressive decoding and shortcut reliance on irrelevant anatomical regions. We introduce Radev, a decision-native multimodal model that integrates anatomy-guided visual compression, direct candidate prediction, and counterfactual confidence supervision. papers.title: Markdown Is Not a Firewall: four coding agents, one rules file, four boundaries
papers.summary: Teams put a one-page rules file in a repository and call it a control on coding agents. A registered study found agents rarely look up a repository's contribution rules. I asked the security question: what does a rules file do at a boundary, against a gate? I tested one 278-word rules file, with hypotheses and analysis code deposited first. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and OpenCode with DeepSeek worked through 20 small repositories with hidden tests, 12 for three of them. papers.title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
papers.summary: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on mode

papers.title: So Many Ways to Multiply 3times3 Matrices: A Large Dataset of Rank-23 Schemes
papers.summary: A publicly available dataset of 62029 rank-23 schemes for 3times3 matrix multiplication is presented. Every scheme in it has its own rank pattern, an invariant formed by the ranks of the factor matrices of a scheme, so all schemes are pairwise inequivalent. The schemes were obtained by a numerical method combining gradient descent with alternating least squares and by flip graph search, and have ternary, integer or rational coefficients.
